data.detail: Shanghai Moonton Technology Co. Ltd. (上海沐瞳科技有限公司) founded July 2014 in Shanghai (Minhang District), China; video game development, publishing and esports company with offices in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Philippines, Latin America, Hong Kong and mainland China

Founders: Xu Zhenhua (Watson Xu), a former Tencent employee who founded Moonton; Yuan Jing also a co-founder and was CEO at the time of the 2021 ByteDance deal; Yuan Jing described as founder interpreting MLBB's rise in Chinese press (ref listed on Wikipedia Moonton page)
data.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonton (refs: Caixin Global 2021-03-24; 36kr/Jakarta Globe ref 'Yuan Jing founder of Mutong Technology')

data.detail: First commercial release: Magic Rush: Heroes (RPG), launched worldwide excluding mainland China in April 2015; listed in Google Play 2015 Best of the Year - Best Strategy Games (per official Moonton company timeline)

MLBB first released 14 July 2016 as 'Mobile Legends: 5v5 MOBA' (Android, distributed by Elex in US); removed after Riot complaint and relaunched as Mobile Legends: Bang Bang on 9 November 2016; official Moonton timeline states MLBB launched worldwide November 2016 excluding mainland China and was listed in Google Play 2016 Best of the Year - Best Competitive Games

Growth milestones: first MLBB offline esports tournament in Indonesia May 2017; inaugural MSC (Southeast Asia Cup) September 2017; MPL launched November 2017 in Indonesia/Malaysia/Singapore; Philippines MPL March 2018; Myanmar MPL February 2019; Singapore branch May 2018; Indonesia branch October 2018

Other titles: Mobile Legends: Adventure (August 2019 worldwide ex-China; Japan/Korea 2021 reaching #1 free charts); Watcher of Realms (July 2023 global; mainland China October 2024); Magic Chess: Go Go (February 2025 APAC); Silver and Blood (June 2025); Acecraft (August 2025); MLBB itself launched in mainland China January 2025 after April 2023 Chinese import approval

Leadership over time: CEO Xu Zhenhua cited during 2017-2018 lawsuits; CEO Yuan Jing at March 2021 ByteDance acquisition; Zhang Yunfan (Yunfan Zhang) appointed CEO May 2024 when ByteDance shelved a planned sale (Bloomberg 2024-05-13; SCMP 2024-05-16)
data.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonton (infobox key people; refs Bloomberg + SCMP)

data.detail: Company scale: 2,000+ employees reported for 2025 (Borneo Bulletin Nov 2023 via Wikipedia infobox); Moonton named National Key Cultural Export Enterprise by China Ministry of Commerce in 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 listings

Original game 'Mobile Legends: 5v5 MOBA' removed from Google Play in 2016 after Riot complained to Google; relaunched as Mobile Legends: Bang Bang on 9 November 2016; Riot also complained the name sounded confusingly similar to League of Legends

Riot Games sued Shanghai Moonton in US District Court C.D. Cal. (case 2:17-cv-04986, filed July 2017; Riot's parent Tencent named in coverage dated 2017-07-12) alleging Mobile Legends copied League of Legends; case dismissed with US court ruling the dispute belonged under Chinese court jurisdiction

Tencent (on behalf of Riot) separately sued Moonton CEO Xu Zhenhua in Shanghai No.1 Intermediate People's Court over non-compete violations; ruled in Tencent's favor July 2018 awarding RMB19.4 million (~US$2.9 million) - reported as largest domestic non-compete award in China at the time

Moonton sued Tencent in China in 2019 for unfair competition/defamation; Moonton won the commercial defamation suit reported October 2022 with compensation reported around 308,000 yuan (~US$30.8K) - single-source (Pandaily), not independently re-verified

Riot Games filed a second US lawsuit against Moonton in May 2022 (C.D. Cal.) claiming MLBB copied expressive elements from League of Legends and Wild Rift; dismissed with court ruling the case should be heard in China

Moonton and Riot Games reached a global settlement ending all IP disputes (2024; reported 2 April 2024): both parties signed a settlement agreement and Riot formally withdrew all related lawsuits after disputes dating back to 2017 (verified directly on ONE Esports article + Wikipedia summary)

India ban: MLBB banned in India 29 June 2020 with other apps of alleged Chinese origin after the China-India skirmishes; returned to India 24 April 2024 as 'Moba Legends: 5v5!' published by Vizta Games (Android)

US ban episode (what actually happened): on ~18-19 January 2025 MLBB went offline in US Apple/Google app stores alongside TikTok, Marvel Snap and other ByteDance/Nuverse-linked apps when the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act took effect; headlines verified via Google News RSS: GamesIndustry.biz 2025-01-20 'Marvel Snap and Mobile Legends: Bang Bang unavailable in US following TikTok ban', esports.gg and PocketGamer.biz and Mobilegamer.biz 2025-01-19; service returned within days - mxdwn Games 2025-01-24 'Mobile Legends Returns to the U.S. After Temporary Ban'; Wikipedia describes it as a brief unenforced ban

US publishing handover: on 26 March 2025 Moonton announced US publishing operations for MLBB transferred to Skystone Games; a US-specific version 'Mobile Legends: Bang Bang US' went live 27 March 2025 following the earlier removal of the original version from US app stores (also stated on Wikipedia Moonton page)
data.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonton (refs: Esports Insider 2025-03-26 'Mobile Legends: Bang Bang moves US publishing operations') + https://www.pocketgamer.biz/skystone-games-takes-us-publishing-rights-for-mobile-legends-as-tiktok-ban-looms

data.detail: July 2021: Moonton reportedly required MLBB esports organizations to sign optional exclusivity contracts barring them from fielding League of Legends: Wild Rift teams (with benefits attached); criticized by Team Secret CEO; ahead of MSC 2025 S8UL Esports was disqualified after two players promoted rival MOBA Honor of Kings

ByteDance agreed to acquire Moonton on 22 March 2021 at a valuation of around US$4 billion (Reuters sources; ByteDance matched a competing Tencent bid); Moonton to operate independently under CEO Yuan Jing; covered by Reuters, CNBC (2021-03-23) and Esports Insider (Tom Daniels, 2021-03-22)
data.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonton (refs: Reuters 'ByteDance acquires gaming studio Moonton at around $4 billion valuation'; CNBC Kharpal 2021-03-23) + https://esportsinsider.com/2021/03/bytedance-acquires-mobile-legends-publisher-moonton-at-a-reported-4bn-valuation

data.detail: CONFLICT NOTE (Wikipedia internal): Wikipedia Moonton lead sentence says 'In October 2021, ByteDance acquired Moonton' while the article body and Reuters/CNBC/Esports Insider date the acquisition agreement to 22 March 2021; October 2021 likely reflects deal completion (ContentAsia eNewsletter 18-24 Oct 2021 cited on Wikipedia) - both dates recorded

By April 2018 MLBB exceeded 200 million total registered accounts (Wikipedia Moonton history section)
As of July 2019 (official Moonton PR Newswire release, fetched directly): MLBB downloaded over 500 million times since 2016, localized into 23 languages, over 75 million monthly users globally

Moonton announced MLBB passed 1 billion cumulative downloads worldwide (ONE Esports article by Amanda Tan, 2020-11-03; official Moonton timeline states October 2020); accompanying official stats: peak monthly active users exceeded 100 million; also announced 9.77 billion matches played and 9.8 million Mythic-rank players (ONE Esports)
By August 2021 total registered accounts exceeded 1 billion (official Moonton timeline + Wikipedia Moonton)

2025 scale (official Moonton about page, fetched 2026-10-22): more than 1.5 billion installations and over 110 million monthly active users across more than 80 countries, top-10 most-played mobile game in 80+ countries; same figures cited on Wikipedia Moonton (refs: Statista 'Mobile Legends revenue worldwide 2025'; Marketing-Interactive 2025-11-03)
18 March 2026: Moonton celebrated a new record high in daily active users (DAU) for MLBB (Wikipedia Moonton history section, ref: Pressroom Philippines)

July 2018: MLBB had generated ~US$200 million in global revenues (PocketGamer.biz, Iain Harris, 20 July 2018 - reference entry verified on Wikipedia Moonton; the pocketgamer.biz article itself returns 403 from this sandbox)

data.detail: Revenue milestones by year from Sensor Tower / AppMagic / data.ai could NOT be verified in this environment: sensortower.com reachable but the MLBB $1B-lifetime-spending article was not located on-site (404s), appmagic.rocks returns 403, Statista paywalled; any specific annual revenue figure beyond the July 2018 $200M is UNVERIFIED for this dataset

Proxy monetization-scale datapoint: Double 11 re-release coverage states Collector-tier draw skins typically cost 2,000-3,000 diamonds (see Monetization rows); Diamond Vault Legend skins guaranteed at ~9,000 diamonds (~US$200) per ONE Esports - indicates diamond-economy pricing scale circa 2023

MLBB is free-to-play monetized through in-app purchases of heroes and cosmetic skins; premium currency is diamonds bought via in-app purchase and third-party top-up channels; Wikipedia describes progression as not pay-to-win

Starlight membership revamp announced 27 January 2023 (effective 1 February 2023): added exclusive Starlight trail effect, first-purchase bundle worth 1700 diamonds, Starlight shop with past skins (e.g. 2021 Water Lily Kagura) and Starlight chests; per ONE Esports the standard Starlight member price then cost 550 diamonds (guarantees exclusive + painted monthly skin) and Starlight member+ (instant level 30) cost 1,100 diamonds
data.image_source: cdn.oneesports.gg (ONE Esports: MLBB Starlight membership revamp)

data.detail: CONFLICT NOTE (Starlight pricing): ONE Esports monthly skin articles state the monthly Starlight skin releases 'for 300 diamonds' (Iron Hound Saber 1 Feb 2023; Twilight Waltz Layla 1 Oct 2023; Nightwalker Melissa 1 Nov 2023) while the revamp article states standard membership costs 550 diamonds - likely skin-alone vs membership pricing; treated as conflicting sourced figures

Starlight history: Saber's Force Warrior was his second Starlight skin and was released in 2016 (per ONE Esports Jan 2023), corroborating the Starlight system existing in 2016; fan compilations list Starlight skins from December 2016, but the official launch year/month of the Starlight Member system itself is UNVERIFIED by trusted press (MLBB Fandom unreachable)

Limited-time draw/lucky-box events are a core monetization format: Double 11 (11 November) re-release events bring back coveted Collector-tier skins which 'typically cost between 2,000 and 3,000 diamonds, with the final price depending on your luck during the event draws' (ONE Esports, November 2023)

Diamond Vault (time-limited dig event for Legend skins): Angelic Agent Lesley was the first Legend skin in the Diamond Vault; one dig cost 100 diamonds, five digs 450; at 100 digs (~9,000 diamonds, ~US$200) the skin was guaranteed (ONE Esports 'rarest skins', January 2023)

Typical Epic (899-diamond list) and Legend (2199-diamond list) skin price tiers are widely cited by fan wikis/guides but were NOT verified against a reachable trusted source in this environment - UNVERIFIED, do not publish as fact
Regional price differences for diamonds (e.g. cheaper SEA top-up channels) are commonly claimed by community sources but no trusted source was reachable to confirm specific examples - UNVERIFIED

Championship honorary skins: each M-Series winning team gets a limited-time purchasable skin of a chosen hero; since M5 the Finals MVP also receives an FMVP skin (first: David 'FlapTzy' Canon, Paquito); December 2021 #WeWantEstes controversy over Moonton citing 'marketability' before reversing and granting Estes for Blacklist International's M3 skin (announced 24 December 2021)

Licensed collaboration skins (limited-time paid events): SNK King of Fighters series from March 2019 (first MLBB collaboration; e.g. Karina as Leona redeemable for free, Guinevere as Athena, Aurora as Kula Diamond, Dyrroth as Orochi Chris, Gusion as K', Chou as Iori Yagami); Star Wars July 2021 (SEA/Japan); Transformers August 2021; Sanrio February 2022; Kung Fu Panda August 2022; Saint Seiya October 2022 (gold skins via draw); KOF third series 2024

Retail/top-up tie-ins: AF Payments (Beep card) partnered Moonton and UniPin (October 2024) for co-branded MLBB transit cards with in-game item codes in the Philippines; J&T Express Malaysia 'Golden Month 2026' campaign awarded diamonds/skins/merchandise

MLBB Creator Camp - official Moonton creator/content program with regional Discord hubs; the EN-PH Creator Camp Discord alone listed ~411,890 members at time of capture (inherited from prior session; discord.com not re-reachable this session)

MLBB Creator Base - official global creator community (@mlbbcreators_official) showing 12M followers / 3M likes on TikTok at time of capture (inherited from prior session; tiktok.com not re-reachable this session); separate from Creator Camp
MLBB runs an official Creator Contest with an identity-verification platform (sg-play.mobilelegends.com) so only verified genuine creators can receive event rewards (inherited from prior session)

Celebrity/ambassador partnerships: Manny Pacquiao announced as MLBB brand ambassador for the Philippines (November 2020) with dedicated hero Paquito; Southeast Asian folklore heroes (Lapu-Lapu, Minsitthar, Kadita, Badang) and Garudayana creator Is Yuniarto collaboration (Gatotkaca, 2017)

MPL Indonesia became the first franchised MLBB/esports league in Southeast Asia at MPL-ID Season 4 (verified directly on official PR Newswire release, 24 July 2019): permanent slot via one-time franchise fee of USD 1 million for eight teams (Alter Ego, Aura, Bigetron, EVOS, Geek Fam, Genflix Aerowolf, ONIC, RRQ); >50% league revenue share to teams before operational/marketing costs borne fully by Moonton; hard salary cap; player minimum salary + 6-month minimum contracts; no relegation; Moonton also committed USD 8 million to develop the Indonesian MLBB esports community
